title: Sounding natural in conversation
point: Soften requests and opinions, and react to what people say, with the small set phrases native speakers use all the time.

sentences.ja: もしよかったら、明日車で送ってもらえないかなと思って。
sentences.text: I was wondering if you could give me a ride tomorrow.
sentences.note: The past "I was wondering" is softer than "I wonder"; it's a polite way to ask a favor.

sentences.ja: 窓、開けてもいいですか？
sentences.text: Would you mind if I opened the window?
sentences.note: To say yes to "Would you mind…", answer "Not at all" or "Go ahead", not "Yes".

sentences.ja: 今日は外食より家で食べたいな。
sentences.text: I'd rather eat in tonight, if that's okay.

sentences.ja: その映画、ちょっと退屈だったかな。
sentences.text: The movie was kind of boring, to be honest.
sentences.note: "Kind of" softens a negative opinion, like Japanese "ちょっと".

sentences.ja: なるほど、それなら納得。
sentences.note: "That makes sense" is the everyday "なるほど"; "I see" alone can sound flat.

sentences.ja: 徹夜したの？どうりで眠そうなわけだ。
sentences.text: You pulled an all-nighter? No wonder you look so tired.

sentences.ja: 行くかどうかは天気次第だね。
sentences.text: Whether we go really depends on the weather.

sentences.ja: えっ、本当に？それはついてなかったね。
sentences.text: Wait, seriously? That's such bad luck.

sentences.ja: 全然いいよ、気にしないで。
sentences.text: Oh, no worries. It's totally fine.
sentences.note: "No worries" answers both thanks and apologies in casual speech.
